2. Important Notice, Scope & Document Governance
Welcome to Asterion Digital Systems. This handbook explains the employment standards and internal processes used at our company. It is designed to provide employees with a consistent reference point.
2.1 Purpose of the handbook
The handbook describes workplace expectations, employee support, compensation administration, working arrangements, information security, performance management and separation procedures. It is intended to help employees understand how the organization operates and where to seek guidance.
2.2 Who must follow it
• All regular full-time and part-time employees, unless a section expressly states otherwise.
• Interns, apprentices, trainees and fixed-term employees must follow conduct, security, attendance and workplace safety requirements. Their compensation and leave entitlements are governed by their individual agreements and applicable law.
• Consultants, vendors and visitors must comply with relevant site, confidentiality and security requirements while on company premises or systems.
2.3 Relationship with employment agreements and law
This handbook is a policy guide and does not replace an appointment letter, employment agreement, statutory notice, benefit plan document or applicable Indian law. Where a contractual term or policy conflicts with mandatory law, the law prevails. Where an individual agreement provides a more favourable lawful entitlement, that agreement will be reviewed by HR.
2.4 Interpretation and policy ownership
The People & Culture Department administers this handbook in consultation with Finance, Legal, Information Security and business leaders. Managers may explain procedures but may not create exceptions to statutory requirements. Any exception to an internal policy must be documented and approved by the authorized function.
2.5 Changes and employee acknowledgement

question: In which year was Asterion Digital Systems established?
actual_answer: Asterion Digital Systems was established in 2017 [Page 3].

3. About Asterion Digital Systems
Asterion Digital Systems Private Limited is an India-based technology and digital engineering services company established in 2017. The organization builds and operates software products and technology solutions for businesses.
3.1 Company profile
Asterion Digital Systems works across product engineering, enterprise application development, cloud modernization, data platforms, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and managed technology services. Its client portfolio includes early-stage companies, mid-sized Indian businesses and selected international enterprises.
3.2 Mission
To make useful technology dependable, secure and accessible by combining thoughtful engineering, responsible innovation and long-term customer partnerships.
3.3 Vision
To become a trusted digital engineering partner recognized for quality delivery, technical depth, ethical conduct and an environment where people can build meaningful careers.
3.4 Core values
• Customer outcomes: understand the problem before proposing a solution; measure success by the value delivered.
• Ownership: take responsibility for commitments, communicate risks early and close the loop.
• Craftsmanship: write maintainable software, test carefully and document important decisions.
• Integrity: be honest about progress, capability, estimates, errors and conflicts of interest.
• Respect: treat colleagues, clients and partners fairly regardless of role or background.
• Learning: share knowledge, seek feedback and improve systems rather than repeating avoidable mistakes.
3.5 Operating principles
Teams are expected to work transparently, use evidence when making decisions, keep customer data secure and avoid unnecessary bureaucracy. Asterion Digital Systems favours small accountable teams, written project decisions and clear escalation paths. Speed is valued, but not at the cost of safety, legality or engineering quality.

4. Services, Expertise & Industry Focus
Asterion Digital Systems's service portfolio is organized around engineering capabilities rather than a single technology stack. Teams may be assigned to internal products, client delivery, research initiatives or long-term support engagements.
4.1 Core service lines
Service line Typical work
Product & application engineering
Web and mobile applications, APIs, platform architecture, testing and maintenance
Cloud & DevOps Cloud migration, infrastructure automation, CI/CD, observability and reliability engineering
AI, data & automation Data pipelines, analytics, machine learning prototypes, retrieval- augmented generation and workflow automation
Cybersecurity Secure development reviews, identity controls, vulnerability management and security assessments
Enterprise integration ERP/CRM integrations, workflow systems, API gateways and legacy modernization
Technology consulting Discovery workshops, architecture reviews, delivery planning and technical due diligence
4.2 Technology expertise
• Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, HTML, CSS and accessible UI engineering.
• Backend: Java, Node.js, Python, REST APIs, event-driven systems and service integration.
• Data: SQL databases, document databases, data modeling, reporting and pipeline orchestration.
• Cloud and platform: containerization, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, monitoring and cloud security fundamentals.
• AI engineering: model integration, evaluation, prompt design, retrieval systems, agent workflows and human review controls.
• Quality engineering: test automation, API testing, performance testing, release validation and defect analysis.
4.3 Industry exposure
Sectors served include financial services, retail and commerce, education technology, healthcare technology, logistics, manufacturing and SaaS. Work in regulated or sensitive sectors may require additional background checks, training, access restrictions and client-specific controls.

15. Internships, Trainees & Graduate Programme
Asterion Digital Systems's early-career programme provides structured exposure to real engineering practices. An internship is a learning and assessment arrangement, not a promise of permanent employment.
15.1 Programme design
Standard internships are planned for three months in software engineering, AI and data, cloud operations, cybersecurity, quality engineering, business analysis or product operations. Each intern receives a written scope, a designated mentor and measurable deliverables.
15.2 Internship terms
Item Arrangement
Duration 3 months
Monthly stipend ₹10,000, subject to signed agreement
Working days Monday to Friday
Weekly holidays Saturday and Sunday
Leave 2 casual leave days per month, subject to agreement
Mentorship Named reporting mentor
Feedback Monthly progress discussion
Completion evidence Certificate after successful completion and deliverable submission
15.3 Intern responsibilities
• Attend agreed sessions and communicate absence promptly.
• Complete assigned learning and project deliverables honestly.
• Use only approved systems and protect company/client information.
• Do not publish project code, screenshots or customer details without written approval.
• Ask for review when blocked and document work so it can be assessed.
15.4 Evaluation
Monthly reviews may assess technical progress, task quality, initiative, communication, reliability, collaboration and ability to respond to feedback. The mentor should provide specific improvement points and a fair opportunity to address gaps.
15.5 Conversion and extension
High-performing interns may be considered for a graduate role where an approved vacancy exists. Conversion is not automatic and depends on business need, interview performance, budget and formal offer approval. Extensions require written approval from the department manager and HR.
No recruitment or internship fee is payable to Asterion Digital Systems at any stage of this programme.

7. Working Hours, Shifts & Attendance
Standard office schedules are designed to support collaboration across teams while allowing predictable personal time. Client or operational roles may follow approved shift arrangements communicated in writing.
7.1 Standard schedule
Item Standard arrangement
Working days Monday to Friday
Core office hours 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM
Meal break 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM
Short breaks Two reasonable 15-minute breaks
Weekly rest days Saturday and Sunday
Expected work time Approximately 40 hours per week, excluding meal break
7.2 Flexible start time
With manager approval, eligible employees may start between 8:00 AM and 11:00 AM and complete the required daily working hours. Employees must still attend mandatory customer meetings, team ceremonies and agreed collaboration windows. Flexibility is a working arrangement, not an entitlement to be unavailable during agreed core hours.
7.3 Attendance recording
• Record attendance through the approved HR portal, access system or designated timekeeping application.
• Remote employees must use the approved attendance workflow and accurately record working time.
• Submit an attendance correction request within 48 hours of discovering an error.
• Repeated unexplained absence, proxy attendance or falsified records may lead to investigation and disciplinary action.
7.4 Late arrival and absence
The standard arrival grace period is until 9:45 AM. More than five late arrivals in a calendar month may trigger a manager discussion and, where appropriate, a formal warning. Employees unable to attend must inform their manager as early as reasonably possible and follow the leave procedure.
7.5 Shift work and overtime

7.5 Shift work and overtime
Certain support, infrastructure and client operations teams may work staggered or rotational shifts. Shift timings, weekly rest and applicable allowances must be documented before the arrangement begins. Overtime must be approved in advance and handled in accordance with applicable law, contract terms and company rules. Employees should not assume that unapproved extra hours automatically qualify for additional payment.

8.5 Review and withdrawal
Managers may review remote arrangements based on delivery, customer feedback, security events, attendance and team needs. A remote arrangement may be temporarily suspended where a role changes, a client requires onsite presence or policy requirements are not met.

Payroll is administered monthly using approved employee records and bank details. Employees should review their payslips and raise discrepancies promptly so that corrections can be assessed within payroll timelines.
10.1 Payroll cycle
Payroll item Policy approach
Payroll period First to last calendar day of each month
Salary payment Normally on the last working day of the month
Payment method Direct transfer to verified employee bank account
Payslip Published in the secure employee portal
Bank holiday Payment is normally processed on the preceding working day
10.2 Variable pay and performance bonus
Where an offer letter includes variable compensation, the applicable plan will state the target amount, measurement period, performance conditions, payment timing and treatment during leave or separation. A target incentive may range from 0% to 15% of annual fixed pay for eligible roles; actual plans vary by role and are not guaranteed unless contractually stated.
10.3 Spot awards and referral awards
The company may operate discretionary recognition awards for exceptional delivery, innovation, customer impact or employee referrals. Eligibility, payout value and tax treatment are governed by the active scheme. Referral awards are payable only after the referred candidate joins and completes the scheme's stated retention period.
10.4 Expense reimbursement
• Obtain prior approval for travel, client entertainment, equipment or training expenses where required.
• Submit itemized receipts and business purpose through the expense portal within 30 days.
• Personal purchases, alcohol where prohibited by policy, fines, upgrades without approval and unsupported claims are not reimbursable.

Onboarding helps new employees understand the company, their role, team expectations and essential controls. Managers are responsible for providing a realistic first-month plan and access to the tools required for the role.
14.1 First 10 working days
Period Core activities
Day 1 Welcome, identity verification, policies, equipment and access setup
Days 2–3 Company overview, team introductions, security and conduct training
Days 4–5 Role objectives, tools, architecture or process walkthrough
Week 2 Starter tasks, mentor check-in, expectations and learning plan
14.2 Probation
The standard probation period is six months unless the offer letter states otherwise. During probation, the manager should review role fit, quality, reliability, communication, learning progress and conduct. Probation may be confirmed, extended with written reasons or ended in accordance with the employment agreement and applicable law.
14.3 Confirmation
Confirmation is communicated in writing by HR after the manager's recommendation and required approvals. Employees should not assume that probation has ended merely because the stated period has elapsed. Any extension should identify the development areas, review date and support available.
14.4 Manager responsibilities
• Set clear 30-, 60- and 90-day outcomes.
• Assign a buddy or mentor where feasible.
• Ensure access is role-appropriate and removed when no longer needed.
• Schedule regular check-ins and provide actionable feedback.
• Explain escalation routes, leave procedures and performance expectations.
14.5 Employee responsibilities
New employees must complete mandatory training, follow security requirements, ask questions when instructions are unclear and promptly report missing access, equipment or support. Employees must not share passwords or use another person's account to bypass access controls.

16. Performance Management, Ratings & Rankings
Performance management is intended to align individual contribution with business outcomes, support development and identify barriers to effective work. Ratings should be evidence-based and calibrated across comparable roles.
16.1 Review cycle
Formal reviews are conducted twice annually: January–June and July–December. Managers should hold regular check-ins throughout the year rather than relying only on review meetings. Employees may submit a self-assessment with examples, outcomes and development goals.
16.2 Evaluation dimensions
Dimension What is assessed
Delivery & ownership Commitment reliability, prioritization, follow-through and outcomes
Quality Correctness, maintainability, testing, documentation and risk awareness
Technical / functional skill Role knowledge, problem-solving and sound judgment
Collaboration Communication, teamwork, review quality and knowledge sharing
Customer impact Responsiveness, service quality and measurable user/client value
Professional conduct Integrity, security, attendance and respectful behaviour
16.3 Rating scale
Rating Label Meaning
5 Exceptional Consistently exceeds role expectations with substantial impact
4 Exceeds expectations Frequently delivers beyond agreed expectations
3 Meets expectations Reliably fulfils the requirements of the role
2 Partially meets Some expectations are missed; improvement plan is needed
1 Does not meet Material and sustained gaps require urgent action
16.4 Internal contribution bands
For talent discussions only, the company may group performance outcomes into contribution bands: Exceptional (top impact), Strong (above role expectations), Solid (meets expectations) and Improvement Required. These are not public employee rankings, do not create guaranteed quotas and must not replace an individual's documented evidence.
16.5 Fairness and review challenge

16.5 Fairness and review challenge
Managers must avoid ranking employees solely by hours online, number of messages, personality similarity or visibility. Employees may request clarification of evidence and submit a written response to HR within 10 working days of receiving the formal review.

17. Promotion, Career Paths & Development
Career growth may occur through deeper technical specialization, broader leadership responsibility, product ownership or movement into another suitable function. Promotion is based on sustained readiness and available organizational need, not tenure alone.
17.1 Career levels
Level Typical scope Example next step
L1 Associate Works with guidance; builds foundational skills
L2 Engineer
L2 Engineer Owns defined tasks and components L3 Senior Engineer
L3 Senior Engineer Owns features or workstreams; mentors peers L4 Lead / Specialist
L4 Lead / Specialist Sets technical direction for a team or domain L5 Manager / Principal
L5 Manager Leads people, delivery or a major function L6 Director
L6 Director Owns multi-team strategy and outcomes Executive leadership
17.2 Promotion readiness
• Consistent performance at the next-level scope, not isolated exceptional work.
• Demonstrated judgment, accountability and ability to handle greater complexity.
• Evidence of collaboration, mentoring or leadership appropriate to the target role.
• A sustained business need and an approved position or role redesign.
• Completion of any required technical, compliance or leadership assessment.
17.3 Development plans
Employees and managers should agree on one to three meaningful development priorities per review cycle. Plans may include project assignments, mentoring, technical learning, communication practice, certification or cross-functional exposure. Progress should be reviewed during regular one- to-one meetings.
17.4 Lateral movement
A lateral move may be appropriate where an employee's strengths align with another team or where the business needs a different skill mix. Transfers should include a transition plan, revised objectives and any necessary training.
17.5 No automatic entitlement

20. Information Security, Privacy & Acceptable Use
Every employee is responsible for protecting company systems, client information and personal data. Security requirements apply whether work is performed from an office, home or customer location.
20.1 Account and password security
• Use unique passwords of at least 12 characters where supported and enable multi-factor authentication.
• Never share passwords, one-time codes, recovery codes or access tokens.
• Use approved password managers and company identity systems.
• Report suspected phishing, credential theft or unauthorized access immediately.
20.2 Device and network security
• Use approved devices for restricted business information.
• Keep operating systems, endpoint protection and applications updated.
• Lock screens when away and protect devices during travel.
• Do not connect unknown removable media or bypass security controls.
• Report a lost or stolen company device to IT/Security within one hour of discovery.
20.3 Data classification and sharing
Information may be classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted. Employees must follow the handling rules for each class. Confidential or Restricted files must not be sent to personal email, unapproved cloud drives, public AI tools or unauthorized recipients.

Employee information may be processed for recruitment, payroll, benefits, attendance, security, legal compliance and business operations. 6. Work Culture & Employee Experience
Asterion Digital Systems aims to maintain a professional, collaborative and delivery-focused culture. Culture is reflected in everyday decisions: how teams communicate, resolve disagreements, share credit, respond to mistakes and protect one another's ability to do good work.
6.1 Expected behaviours
• Be clear and respectful in meetings, written messages and code reviews.
• Share progress and blockers early; do not hide delays until a deadline has passed.
• Disagree with ideas using evidence, not personal attacks or status.
• Give credit to contributors and document reusable knowledge.
• Respect focus time, time zones, leave and reasonable boundaries outside working hours.
• Raise safety, ethical, security or quality concerns without fear of retaliation.
6.2 Collaboration practices
Teams may use daily or periodic stand-ups, sprint planning, design reviews, retrospectives, one-to- one meetings and written status updates. Meetings should have a purpose, an owner and an expected outcome. Decisions affecting scope, architecture, security or delivery dates should be recorded in an approved workspace.
6.3 Feedback and psychological safety
Managers should provide specific, timely and actionable feedback. Employees may ask for clarification, request a private discussion or use the grievance process where feedback becomes humiliating, discriminatory or retaliatory. Psychological safety does not remove accountability; it enables people to report risks and learn from mistakes.
6.4 Inclusion and accessibility
The company prohibits discrimination and harassment on grounds protected by applicable law. Reasonable workplace adjustments may be discussed confidentially with HR. Team events and internal communications should be planned with accessibility, dietary needs and varied personal circumstances in mind.
6.5 Recognition

6.5 Recognition
Recognition may include peer appreciation, project acknowledgements, learning opportunities, internal awards or performance-linked rewards. Recognition is not a substitute for fair pay, safe working conditions or consistent management.

13. Recruitment, Selection & Employment Checks
Recruitment decisions should be based on role requirements, demonstrated skills, relevant experience and fair assessment. Hiring managers and recruiters must communicate accurately and protect candidate information.
13.1 Recruitment stages
• Role approval and job description: business need, level, reporting line and budget are confirmed.
• Application screening: qualifications and relevant experience are reviewed against the role criteria.
• Assessment: technical, functional, writing or case-based exercises may be used where relevant.
• Interview: structured discussion with role-related questions and consistent evaluation criteria.
• Reference or background checks: performed only where appropriate, lawful and disclosed.
• Offer and acceptance: written terms, compensation, joining date and conditions are shared by authorized HR.
13.2 Fair selection
Candidates must not be asked for payment, deposits or purchases as a condition of recruitment. Interviewers must avoid discriminatory questions unrelated to legitimate job requirements. Assessment tasks should be proportionate and should not be used to obtain unpaid production work.
13.3 Verification
Subject to applicable law and candidate consent where required, the company may verify identity, education, employment history, professional credentials and references. Any discrepancy should be reviewed fairly, with an opportunity for the candidate to clarify material information.
13.4 Offer and joining documents
The offer letter will identify job title, work location, reporting manager, compensation, employment category, probation terms, notice period and any role-specific conditions. Employees must submit accurate joining documents through the approved secure channel.

question: What are the stages of the recruitment process?
expected_answer: Role approval and job description, application screening, assessment, interview, reference or background checks, and offer and acceptance.
actual_answer:
The recruitment process includes the following stages:

- Role approval and job description – confirming business need, level, reporting line and budget.  
- Application screening – reviewing qualifications and relevant experience against the role criteria.  
- Assessment – using technical, functional, writing or case‑based exercises where relevant.

Performance management is intended to align individual contribution with business outcomes, support development and identify barriers to effective work. Ratings should be evidence-based and calibrated across comparable roles.

Formal reviews are conducted twice annually: January–June and July–December. Managers should hold regular check-ins throughout the year rather than relying only on review meetings. Employees may submit a self-assessment with examples, outcomes and development goals.

16.3 Rating scale
Rating Label Meaning
5 Exceptional Consistently exceeds role expectations with substantial impact
4 Exceeds expectations Frequently delivers beyond agreed expectations
3 Meets expectations Reliably fulfils the requirements of the role
2 Partially meets Some expectations are missed; improvement plan is needed
1 Does not meet Material and sustained gaps require urgent action
16.4 Internal contribution bands
For talent discussions only, the company may group performance outcomes into contribution bands: Exceptional (top impact), Strong (above role expectations), Solid (meets expectations) and Improvement Required. Employees are expected to act honestly, lawfully and professionally. The code applies to company premises, remote work, customer sites, work-related events and use of company systems.
19.1 Prohibited conduct
• Harassment, discrimination, bullying, threats or retaliation.
• Falsifying attendance, expenses, qualifications, project records or performance data.
• Unauthorized disclosure of company, employee or client information.
• Misuse, theft or intentional damage of company property or systems.
• Bribery, kickbacks, improper gifts or undisclosed vendor benefits.
• Use of company systems for unlawful activity or unauthorized commercial activity.
• Misrepresenting work completed, source code ownership or professional experience.
19.2 Conflicts of interest
Employees must disclose personal, financial or family interests that could influence business decisions. Examples include selecting a relative's business as a vendor, holding a material interest in a competitor, using confidential information for personal gain or supervising a close relative without safeguards.
19.3 Gifts and hospitality
Employees must not request or accept cash, loans, personal discounts or benefits in exchange for business decisions. Modest customary gifts may be accepted only where lawful, transparent and permitted by the active gifts policy. Anything that could create an obligation or appear to influence judgment must be declined and reported.
19.4 Outside work and intellectual property

19. Code of Conduct, Ethics & Conflicts of Interest
Employees are expected to act honestly, lawfully and professionally. The code applies to company premises, remote work, customer sites, work-related events and use of company systems.
19.1 Prohibited conduct

• Falsifying attendance, expenses, qualifications, project records or performance data.
• Unauthorized disclosure of company, employee or client information.
• Misuse, theft or intentional damage of company property or systems.
• Bribery, kickbacks, improper gifts or undisclosed vendor benefits.
• Use of company systems for unlawful activity or unauthorized commercial activity.
• Misrepresenting work completed, source code ownership or professional experience.
19.2 Conflicts of interest
Employees must disclose personal, financial or family interests that could influence business decisions. Examples include selecting a relative's business as a vendor, holding a material interest in a competitor, using confidential information for personal gain or supervising a close relative without safeguards.
19.3 Gifts and hospitality
Employees must not request or accept cash, loans, personal discounts or benefits in exchange for business decisions. Modest customary gifts may be accepted only where lawful, transparent and permitted by the active gifts policy. Anything that could create an obligation or appear to influence judgment must be declined and reported.
19.4 Outside work and intellectual property
Employees must obtain written approval before taking outside employment, consulting or commercial work that may conflict with company duties, use company resources or affect performance. Inventions and work product created within the scope of employment are governed by the employment agreement and applicable law.
